public_rationale: He wrote that nobody 'seems' to make money from GPUs other than NVIDIA and resellers. That is a hedged impression, and it names no measure. Results differ by measure: CoreWeave, for example, made a small operating profit but a net loss in Q2 2025. Big cloud firms do not report profit from AI separately. Scoring this would mean choosing a profit measure and a set of companies he did not name. So the claim is not scored.
limitations: A firmer version of this claim, with a stated measure, could be tested against neocloud and hyperscaler filings.

statement.excerpt: Despite hundreds of billions of GPUs sold, nobody seems to make any money, other than NVIDIA, the company that makes them, and resellers like Dell and Supermicro who buy the GPUs, put them in servers, and sell them to other people.

from_speaker: Despite hundreds of billions of GPUs sold
nobody seems to make any money

our_interpretation: He hedges this as an impression ('nobody seems to make any money'), not a firm statement that every GPU buyer loses money.

'Make any money' has no stated measure (net profit, operating profit, gross profit on GPU services, or AI-specific segment profit). The scope of 'nobody' is also open: GPU operators only, or also chip suppliers and cloud firms.
Big cloud firms do not report AI-specific profit. So the impression cannot be cleanly confirmed or refuted from public filings without supplying a measure and scope he did not give.
Turning this into a firm profitability test would add a precision he did not commit to. It is therefore not scored.
criteria.support_condition: Not scored. A scored test would need a firm claim with a stated measure, for example that no company operating GPUs reported a profit on AI compute.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not scored, for the same reason.
